sections.h2: Which Heard County tax office should I call first?
sections.html:
Two rooms in the Administration Building in Franklin split the work. Room 300 takes payments. Room 400 sets parcel values and approves exemptions. Walking into the wrong one costs an afternoon.

Heard County tax offices at the Franklin administration building

Tax Commissioner201 Park Avenue, Room 300, Franklin, GA 30217; letters to P.O. Box 519(706) 675-3391Weekdays 8:00 AM to 4:45 PM
Board of Tax Assessors201 Park Avenue, Room 400, Franklin, GA 30217; letters to P.O. Box 476(706) 675-3786Weekdays 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM, shut for lunch at noon until 1:00 PM

The Tax Commissioner's counter began staying open through lunch on September 1, 2026. The assessors did not announce the same change, so schedule an assessor visit outside the noon hour. The commissioner's email is heardtc@heardcountyga.com and the assessors answer at heardtax@heardcountyga.com.

sections.h2: How did Heard County, Georgia, take shape?
sections.html:
Georgia carved Heard County out of Carroll, Coweta and Troup counties in 1830, giving it 301 square miles. Its history page calls it the state's seventy-seventh county, and it says Creek holdings were lost under the 1825 Treaty of Indian Springs. State land lotteries then placed settlers on the parcels, mostly families moving within Georgia in search of better ground.

Franklin, named for Benjamin Franklin, existed as a village by 1770 and gained a charter in 1831. Fire destroyed the first courthouse in 1893, a replacement opened in 1894, and the building in use now replaced that one in 1964. Centralhatchee incorporated in 1903 and Ephesus in 1964. Stony ground discouraged big farms, so households lived by subsistence farming until cotton brought a period of relative prosperity once the war ended. The boll weevil, a falling cotton market and the Great Depression pushed many families out, and the people who stayed turned to timber.

That history still shows on the map. Today a large share of acreage is held for lumber, beside a few beef and poultry producers and some factory work. A seller with a wooded tract is dealing with land-use questions that a seller with a Franklin city lot never meets.

sections.h2: What do Heard County housing numbers look like?
sections.html:
Census QuickFacts lists 12,149 residents for Heard in July 2025, a 6.5% gain on the 2020 base of 11,410. Land area is 295.97 square miles, which worked out to 38.6 residents per square mile at the 2020 count. Owner-occupied homes carried a median value of $186,800, and renters paid a median of $917 a month.

  • 4,979 housing units and 4,309 households.
  • Homeowners occupy 72.3% of homes.
  • Permits issued during 2025: 54.
  • Persons aged 65 and over: 17.8%.
  • Persons in poverty: 12.5%.
  • Share who stayed in the same house for a full year: 93.2%.
  • Employer establishments in 2023: 120.

Few households move in a given year, and only 54 permits were issued countywide in 2025. A listing here usually competes with older resale houses and country properties. Workers spend 34.9 minutes getting to work on average, a long drive that suggests many residents earn their pay outside the county.

sections.h2: Why does a Heard County field visit matter before I list?
sections.html:
The assessors' office exists to settle taxability, value and equalization, to mail owners a notice when a value moves, and to approve the exemptions people claim. A county press release dated March 12, 2026 told owners that field staff would be visiting each parcel to update the digest. They take a front photo and a rear photo of every structure and log changes since the previous countywide update. Heard says the state requires this cycle every three years.

Crews carry county identification and vehicle markings. A door hanger is left when nobody answers, so the owner can confirm the interior description. Before you list, phone (706) 675-3786 and ask what the card on your parcel says about bedrooms, baths, outbuildings and finished space. A garage that was converted years ago but still appears as a garage on the record can pull the value in the wrong direction, and a correction before the notice goes out costs you nothing.

  • The valuation date is January 1, and the taxable share is 40% of fair market value.
  • The assessors point owners to a qpublic portal for parcel records.
  • Returns of value are accepted from January 1 until April 1.

sections.h2: What can I do if my Heard County value seems too high?
sections.html:
Put your objection in writing to the Board of Tax Assessors. You get 45 days counted from the mailing date on the notice, and the grounds can be taxability, value, uniformity or an exemption the county denied. State revenue officials cannot override the county on one parcel, so the form should not go to Atlanta.

The uniform PT-311A form asks you to pick a route up front.

  • Board of Equalization: the common choice. The assessors can change the number and mail a fresh notice, which you may contest for another 30 days.
  • Hearing officer: reserved for non-homestead property above $500,000.
  • Arbitration: disputes over value alone, with a certified appraisal due 45 days after the board acknowledges your filing.

A dispute that survives can go on to superior court after written notice within 30 days of the ruling, and the previous year's tax has to be paid first. Complaints about the size of the bill are outside an appeal because elected bodies set the millage rate on their own.

sections.h2: Which 2025 homestead and millage changes affected Heard County owners?
sections.html:
Two items on the county site are worth knowing. First, House Bill 92, signed April 1, 2025, lets owners file a homestead application while the 45-day appeal window is open after assessment notices go out. The Assessor's Office takes it, and you should bring photo ID showing your current address. Second, the Board of Commissioners advertised in 2025 that its tentative millage meant an 18.29 percent rise in collections: 6.467 mills against a rollback figure of 5.467.

Public hearings were held September 15 and September 23, 2025. The Tax Commissioner page posts a History of Tax Levy document for the year, which helps when you price a listing. Skip the homestead filing on a house you live in and the state treats the exemption as waived. April 1 is the usual deadline for a first-time filer.

sections.h2: Who owes Heard County tax when a house sells?
sections.html:
Whoever holds title on January 1 owes that year, and Georgia refunds nothing to someone who sells early in the year. Heard's commissioner page prints no due date, so read your bill or call (706) 675-3391. The statewide default is December 20, though a county may pick December 1, November 15 or installment billing. Interest does not start until 60 days after the postmark on the bill.

Unpaid tax can lead to a recorded lien and then a public auction. The county page carries a 2025 tax sale list revised October 17, 2025, plus older lists. After an auction, Georgia's consumer office says the owner has twelve months to redeem by paying the winning bid, later taxes and assessments, and a 20% premium. Anyone who inherits a house in that position should phone the commissioner early and get the payoff confirmed in writing.

faqs.q: Where can I pay a Heard County tax bill?
faqs.a: Pay at Room 300, 201 Park Avenue, Franklin, or send a check to P.O. Box 519, Franklin, GA 30217. The phone is (706) 675-3391. Weekday hours run 8:00 AM to 4:45 PM, with no lunch closure since September 1, 2026.

faqs.q: Who decides what my Heard County house is worth?
faqs.a: The Board of Tax Assessors, in Room 400 at the same address, phone (706) 675-3786. The commissioner's office only bills, so value disputes go to the assessors.

faqs.q: How much time do I have to contest a Heard County assessment?
faqs.a: You have 45 days beginning on the date the notice was mailed. A new notice opens a new window. File with the county assessors, not the state revenue department.

faqs.q: Can I add a Heard County homestead exemption after April 1?
faqs.a: Sometimes. House Bill 92, signed April 1, 2025, opened the 45-day appeal period after notices are mailed to homestead filings. Bring photo ID with your current address to the Assessor's Office.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Heard County house that has back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as the lien is paid off at the sale. Request a payoff figure from the closing agent before signing day. If an auction has already happened, Georgia allows twelve months to redeem at the bid plus a 20% premium and other charges.
